summary: Evaluation of 14 days of Nightscout telemetry for an automated closed-loop (AAPS) user reveals an 86.0% Time in Range, with 8.9% Time Above Range and 5.1% Time Below Range. Glycemic patterns show afternoon postprandial hyperglycemia peaks and nocturnal/early morning hypoglycemia dips. The user operates with SMB and UAM enabled, dynamic sensitivity at 70%, and an absence of explicit carbohydrate entry data, relying entirely on automation to manage meals alongside concurrent GLP-1 therapy.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM stream is robust with 98.7% coverage over 14 days and minimal gaps. Treatment data includes extensive insulin and pump events, though carbohydrate entries are absent.
analysis_steps.evidence: 3995 CGM entries, 2315 total treatments, 655 insulin entries totalling 275.95 U, coverage 98.7%.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of explicit meal carbohydrate treatment entries limits precise postprandial CR evaluation.

analysis_steps.findings: Good overall TIR (86.0%), but notable nocturnal and early morning hypoglycemia (5.1% <70 mg/dL) and afternoon hyperglycemia peaks (>180 mg/dL up to 32.1% in peak hours).
analysis_steps.evidence: Hourly glucose and daily summaries showing glucose minimums in the 40s/50s mg/dL overnight and maximums reaching 293 mg/dL in the afternoon.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight basal delivery appears slightly strong during early nocturnal hours (00:00–02:00), driving frequent dips below 70 mg/dL. Afternoon basal/automation may be insufficient for post-lunch glucose rises.
analysis_steps.evidence: Local hourly glucose averages showing 11.4% to 18.5% time below range between 00:00 and 02:00, and afternoon averages reaching 162.8 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Unannounced meals make it difficult to isolate pure basal drift from unrecorded meal absorption.

analysis_steps.findings: Profile uses a flat ISF of 56 mg/dL/U across all times, which is heavily supplemented by AAPS dynamic sensitivity scaling (70% adjustment factor). DIA is 10 hours.
analysis_steps.evidence: Active AAPS profile configuration (isf_segments, carb_ratio_segments, dia_hours = 10.0).
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Absence of declared meal carb entries prevents direct validation of CR segments.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are both enabled with smb_always_enabled=true, supporting unannounced-carb handling. However, enabling SMBs during temporary targets combined with aggressive UAM microbolusing contributes to insulin stacking.
analysis_steps.evidence: aaps_profile.smb_settings configuration showing smb_always_enabled=true, uam_enabled=true, smb_with_temp_target_enabled=true.

analysis_steps.findings: Autosens is disabled while Dynamic ISF is active (70%). Safety limits (max basal 12 U/h, max IOB 25 U) are very generous and permit large automated insulin delivery responses.
analysis_steps.evidence: aaps_profile.smb_settings.raw_settings showing autosens_enabled=false, dynamic_sensitivity_enabled=true, max_basal_u_per_hour=12.0, max_iob_units=25.0.

analysis_steps.findings: Meals are unannounced in the telemetry, causing AAPS to rely entirely on UAM and SMBs, resulting in reactive insulin stacking and late correction swings.
analysis_steps.evidence: Treatment summary shows 0 carb entries; loop telemetry records frequent UAM/SMB interventions during glucose rises.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of meal carb and prebolus records.

analysis_steps.findings: Concurrent GLP-1 therapy (1.25 mg doses) slows gastric emptying and causes delayed postprandial absorption peaks that conflict with aggressive early UAM microbolusing.
analysis_steps.evidence: Representative events log GLP-1 1.25mg administration on Aug 14, Aug 17, and Aug 20.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Exact nutritional composition of meals is unknown.

analysis_steps.findings: Telemetry and profile analysis indicate stable overall control with specific vulnerabilities: early nocturnal hypoglycemia and afternoon postprandial hyperglycemia driven by unannounced meals and GLP-1 delayed absorption. All baseline profile and automation settings should be kept while verifying meal logging and observing loop response.
analysis_steps.evidence: Combined evidence from data quality, safety overview, basal/target analysis, automation settings, and GLP-1 treatment notes.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Consistent recording of meal carbohydrate entries.

strengths: High overall Time in Range (86.0%) maintained over the 14-day evaluation period.
Robust CGM data coverage (98.7%) with low gap frequency.
Effective closed-loop automation (AAPS oref1 with Dynamic ISF and SMB/UAM) successfully preventing prolonged severe hyperglycemia.
issues: Nocturnal and early morning hypoglycemia (5.1% <70 mg/dL, with hourly averages showing up to 18.5% below range between 00:00 and 02:00).
Afternoon postprandial hyperglycemia peaks (time above range reaching 32.1% during local hour 16:00).
Absence of manual meal carbohydrate entries leading to heavy reliance on UAM and subsequent insulin stacking during delayed absorption under GLP-1 therapy.

recommendations.title: Monitor Early Nocturnal Basal Delivery
recommendations.description: Observe early night glucose levels (00:00–02:00) where time below range reaches 10%–18.5%, to determine if early basal rates or residual evening correction overlap with resting requirements.

suggested_change.rationale: Data shows nocturnal dips, but changes should be withheld until verifying whether evening corrections or meal overlaps contribute to the dips.

recommendations.title: Evaluate Meal Logging for Automation Support
recommendations.description: Begin logging carbohydrate entries for meals to help AAPS calculate expected insulin requirements and reduce reliance solely on UAM reactive microbolusing.

suggested_change.rationale: Enables better loop prediction accuracy under GLP-1 delayed gastric emptying.

profile_recommendation.rationale: Current profile settings and automation parameters achieve an 86.0% TIR. While nocturnal dips and afternoon spikes exist, they are primarily driven by unannounced meals and GLP-1 delayed absorption rather than fundamental profile defects. Simultaneous parameter changes should be avoided.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Monitor overnight glucose levels (00:00–03:00) and log meal carbohydrate entries for 7 days to assess the impact of unannounced meals versus automated UAM delivery.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep current profile settings and automation configurations unchanged while establishing consistent meal logging.

meal_strategy_summary.rationale: In the absence of declared meal carbohydrate entries, AAPS relies on SMB always enabled and UAM to manage unannounced meals. Under GLP-1 therapy, gastric emptying is delayed, which can lead to late postprandial rises and reactive insulin stacking if automation reacts too aggressively early on.
meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Institute manual meal announcements with a standard prebolus (15–20 minutes) when possible, maintain UAM and SMB as safety nets with moderated aggression, and utilize extended carbohydrates (e-carbs) with 2–4 hour durations for slow-digesting meals or late postprandial rises under GLP-1 therapy.

exceptions.pattern: Afternoon delayed postprandial rise due to GLP-1 delayed gastric emptying.
exceptions.suggestion: Apply e-carbs or a temporary target ahead of known afternoon meal absorption curves.
exceptions.rationale: Prevents aggressive early UAM microbolusing when food absorption is significantly delayed.

exceptions.suggestion: Use temporary targets or review evening correction timing.
exceptions.rationale: Mitigates overlap between residual evening insulin action and resting basal requirements.

meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log carbohydrate entries for at least a subset of meals over a 7-day period to measure actual postprandial CR efficacy and improve loop prediction accuracy.

implementation_steps: Verify current AAPS profile settings and automation status in Nightscout.
Begin recording meal carbohydrate entries and prebolus timing for a 7-day observation period.
Monitor nocturnal glucose levels (00:00–03:00) to evaluate whether early night dips persist independently of evening corrections.
Review postprandial glucose trajectories with the care team before adjusting any basal or CR parameters.
education: AAPS closed-loop automation relies on accurate carbohydrate inputs and insulin sensitivity parameters to predict and smooth glucose excursions.

GLP-1 receptor agonists slow gastric emptying, shifting carbohydrate absorption curves later and requiring adjusted prebolus timing or extended carbohydrate settings to prevent early insulin stacking and late hyperglycemia.
